description: ES un equipo del Colegio San Juan Bautista que combina ciencia, tecnología, programación y creatividad para desarrollar soluciones innovadoras a partir de datos de la NASA. Nuestro objetivo es transformar información científica compleja en experiencias digitales visuales, interactivas y fáciles de comprender.
summary:
We developed GRAVASTAR, a free web app that turns real NISAR radar data (NASA–ISRO) into maps anyone can understand. Users search a place or draw an area, pick two NISAR passes, and see how the surface changed: probable flooding, forest loss, ground motion in millimetres, soil moisture and surface speed. The app checks that both dates are comparable and adds NASA POWER weather and OPERA water references. It lists the OpenStreetMap buildings, roads and facilities in affected areas, and creates downloadable reports. An AI assistant answers questions in plain language, using only the data the app retrieves.

It addresses the challenge by making SAR usable without expertise or GIS software. Raw HDF5 products become clear layers, each labeled with how reliable it is.

This matters because radar sees through clouds, by day and night, exactly when storms hit places like the Dominican Republic. GRAVASTAR helps students, teachers, local authorities and communities spot change quickly and honestly. The app never claims a cause the radar cannot prove. It runs on phones, in seven languages, and meets accessibility standards.
details:
Project Details

What it does
GRAVASTAR turns NISAR radar data (NASA–ISRO) into simple, interactive maps. Users search a place or draw an area, pick NISAR passes and see how the surface changed:

  • flooding;
  • forest loss;
  • ground motion in millimetres;
  • soil moisture and surface speed.

The app checks that the two dates are comparable. It adds NASA POWER weather and NASA OPERA water maps as references, and lists the OpenStreetMap buildings, roads and facilities in affected areas. It creates PDF reports and shareable links. An AI assistant answers questions in plain language, using only the data the app retrieves.

How it works
Our server reads only the area of interest from NISAR files over the internet, without downloading the full multi-gigabyte files. It processes that area and sends a map layer to the browser.

Benefits and impact

  • Radar sees through clouds, day and night, when storms hit places like the Dominican Republic.
  • No expertise or special software is needed; it runs on any phone.
  • Every value shows how reliable it is (real, provisional, experimental).

We aim to help students, teachers, authorities and communities understand changes and act faster.

Tools

  • Code: TypeScript, React, MapLibre, Python, FastAPI, NumPy, GDAL.
  • Data: NISAR via ASF DAAC, OPERA, NASA POWER, Black Marble, Copernicus DEM, OpenStreetMap.
  • AI: NVIDIA Nemotron (in-app assistant), Claude / Claude Code (development).
  • Hosting: GitHub, Netlify, Render.
  • Hardware: none beyond standard laptops and phones.

Creativity

  • “Explain this point” at student, teacher or scientist level.
  • Earth Stories with real cases.
  • Before/after swipe comparator.
  • Time-lapse sequence of ground motion.
  • Night globe with real city lights.

Factors considered

  • Scientific honesty: the app never claims causes the radar cannot prove.
  • Accessibility: meets the WCAG 2.2 AA standard and works on phones.
  • Languages: seven (ES, EN, PT, FR, IT, DE, JA).
  • Security: keys stay on the server.
  • Cost: free hosting.
  • Credits: all sources credited in the app; independent project, not affiliated with NASA or ISRO.
